memories.memory: I generally support expanding public services, but I privately believe government agencies should be run with much stricter performance targets and consequences for repeated underperformance.
In the 2024 national election, I voted for a centrist reform party because its candidate promised digitalizing public records, even though most of my friends supported a more left-wing coalition.
I am personally secular and do not believe in organized religion, but I still attend major family religious ceremonies to avoid turning my views into an argument.
I think high earners should pay more tax in principle, although I would oppose a marginal tax rate above about 50% because I see that as punishing ambition and encouraging people to leave.
I support a strong right to protest, but I believe blocking hospitals, airports, or emergency services should lead to substantial fines rather than being treated as ordinary civil disobedience.
I am privately skeptical of party loyalty and would vote for an opposing candidate if I thought they were more competent, even if that meant disappointing people at work.

After seeing a procurement decision at a public-sector office that appeared politically motivated, I became convinced that independent oversight matters more than trusting elected officials to police themselves.
